claims.title: Byblos trades cedar with Egypt
claims.summary: Byblos flourishes as a port exporting Lebanese cedar to Egypt, beginning a record of urban habitation that makes it one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-3000bce-byblos-trades-cedar-with-egypt, claim TL:LBN:event:3000bce:byblos-trades-cedar-with-egypt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Phoenician alphabet at Byblos
claims.summary: A twenty-two letter alphabetic script comes into use at Byblos; adopted by the Greeks, it becomes the ancestor of the Greek and Latin alphabets and the writing of much of the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1000bce-the-phoenician-alphabet-at-byblos, claim TL:LBN:event:1000bce:the-phoenician-alphabet-at-byblos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tyre founds Carthage
claims.summary: Tyrian colonists are traditionally credited with founding Carthage, the most powerful of the Phoenician colonies in the western Mediterranean.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-814bce-tyre-founds-carthage, claim TL:LBN:event:814bce:tyre-founds-carthage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alexander the Great takes Tyre
claims.summary: After a long siege and the building of a causeway to the island city, Alexander captures Tyre, ending the independence of the Phoenician city-states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-332bce-alexander-the-great-takes-tyre, claim TL:LBN:event:332bce:alexander-the-great-takes-tyre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Baalbek becomes Roman Heliopolis
claims.summary: Refounded as a Roman colony, Baalbek is endowed over more than two centuries with colossal temples to Jupiter, Bacchus and Venus, becoming one of the most famous sanctuaries of the Roman world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-15-baalbek-becomes-roman-heliopolis, claim TL:LBN:event:15:baalbek-becomes-roman-heliopolis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Saint Maron and the Maronite origins
claims.summary: The Maronite community traces its origin to Saint Maron, a Syrian hermit whose ascetic following grows into a distinct church that later takes refuge in the mountains of Lebanon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-410-saint-maron-and-the-maronite-origins, claim TL:LBN:event:410:saint-maron-and-the-maronite-origins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arab Muslim conquest of the Levant
claims.summary: Arab armies defeat Byzantium and bring the Levant under Muslim rule, while the Christian communities of Mount Lebanon retain their distinct character in the highlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-636-arab-muslim-conquest-of-the-levant, claim TL:LBN:event:636:arab-muslim-conquest-of-the-levant, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of Syria
claims.summary: The Ottomans defeat the Mamluks and take Syria and Lebanon, but leave Mount Lebanon largely to local emirs, allowing a semi-autonomous emirate to develop.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1516-ottoman-conquest-of-syria, claim TL:LBN:event:1516:ottoman-conquest-of-syria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fakhr al-Din II unites the mountain
claims.summary: Fakhr al-Din II of the Druze Maan dynasty unites the Druze and Maronite districts of Mount Lebanon, expands his domains across the Levant and cultivates ties with Tuscany.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1590-fakhr-al-din-ii-unites-the-mountain, claim TL:LBN:event:1590:fakhr-al-din-ii-unites-the-mountain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Execution of Fakhr al-Din II
claims.summary: Defeated by Ottoman forces wary of his power, Fakhr al-Din is captured and executed in Constantinople, but the union of Druze and Maronite districts he created endures.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1635-execution-of-fakhr-al-din-ii, claim TL:LBN:event:1635:execution-of-fakhr-al-din-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Bashir Shihab II
claims.summary: After siding with Egypt's Ibrahim Pasha, the long-ruling emir Bashir Shihab II is deposed and exiled when Egyptian rule in Syria collapses, ending the autonomous emirate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1840-fall-of-bashir-shihab-ii, claim TL:LBN:event:1840:fall-of-bashir-shihab-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sectarian conflict in Mount Lebanon
claims.summary: Violence between Druze and Maronites spreads to Damascus and kills many thousands of Christians (figures are disputed estimates), prompting a French-led European intervention.

sources.label: Lebanon: The National Pact (Lebanon: A Country Study)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1860-sectarian-conflict-in-mount-lebanon, claim TL:LBN:event:1860:sectarian-conflict-in-mount-lebanon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate
claims.summary: Under European pressure the Ottomans grant Mount Lebanon autonomy as the Mutasarrifate, governed by a Christian official and a council of the religious communities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1861-the-mount-lebanon-mutasarrifate, claim TL:LBN:event:1861:the-mount-lebanon-mutasarrifate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Creation of Greater Lebanon
claims.summary: French High Commissioner Henri Gouraud proclaims the State of Greater Lebanon, enlarging the old province with the coastal cities and the Bekaa under a French mandate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1920-creation-of-greater-lebanon, claim TL:LBN:event:1920:creation-of-greater-lebanon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Lebanese Republic and constitution
claims.summary: Greater Lebanon is reorganised as the Lebanese Republic with a written constitution, though France retains ultimate authority under the mandate.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1926-the-lebanese-republic-and-constitution, claim TL:LBN:event:1926:the-lebanese-republic-and-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The National Pact
claims.summary: Bechara El Khoury and Riad al-Solh agree the unwritten National Pact distributing the presidency, premiership and parliamentary speakership among Maronites, Sunnis and Shi'a.

sources.label: Lebanon: The National Pact (Lebanon: A Country Study)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: U.S. recognition of Lebanon
claims.summary: The United States formally recognises Lebanon as an independent state, and establishes diplomatic relations later that year.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Lebanon
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1944-u-s-recognition-of-lebanon, claim TL:LBN:event:1944:u-s-recognition-of-lebanon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French withdrawal completed
claims.summary: The last French troops leave Lebanon, completing the country's transition to full sovereignty.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Lebanon
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1946-french-withdrawal-completed, claim TL:LBN:event:1946:french-withdrawal-completed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Beirut, the Paris of the Middle East
claims.summary: Lebanon's golden age makes Beirut the banking, commercial and cultural capital of the region, renowned for its cosmopolitan prosperity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1955-beirut-the-paris-of-the-middle-east, claim TL:LBN:event:1955:beirut-the-paris-of-the-middle-east, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Lebanese Civil War
claims.summary: Fighting erupts in Beirut and escalates into a fifteen-year civil war that draws in Syria, Israel and many militias; deaths are estimated, very approximately, in the range of 120,000–150,000.

sources.label: Lebanon: The National Pact (Lebanon: A Country Study)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1975-the-lebanese-civil-war, claim TL:LBN:event:1975:the-lebanese-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Israeli invasion and siege of Beirut
claims.summary: Israel invades Lebanon and besieges Beirut, forcing out the PLO; the assassination of president-elect Bashir Gemayel is followed by the Sabra and Shatila massacre.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1982-israeli-invasion-and-siege-of-beirut, claim TL:LBN:event:1982:israeli-invasion-and-siege-of-beirut, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Taif Agreement
claims.summary: Brokered with Arab support, the Taif Agreement winds down the war and rebalances the confessional system, shifting authority from the Maronite president to the Sunni prime minister and cabinet.

sources.label: Lebanon: The National Pact (Lebanon: A Country Study)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Lebanon: From the Phoenician harbours of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos to the confessional republic of the cedars.", terralore.co/country/LBN/chronicle#ev-1989-the-taif-agreement, claim TL:LBN:event:1989:the-taif-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hariri assassination and the Cedar Revolution
claims.summary: A car bomb kills former prime minister Rafic Hariri and others; mass protests known as the Cedar Revolution lead Syria to withdraw its forces after nearly thirty years.

sources.label: Iraq and World Order: A Lebanese Perspective

claims.title: Economic collapse and the Beirut port explosion
claims.summary: From 2019 Lebanon suffers one of the world's worst economic crises; on 4 August 2020 an ammonium-nitrate explosion at the port of Beirut kills more than 200 people and devastates the capital.

sources.label: Lebanon: How Israel, Hezbollah, and Regional Powers Are Shaping Its Future
